concepts.title: A — Source cards, separate actions
concepts.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Edit the supplied native L5R Emperor game screenshot into a polished UI CONCEPT. Preserve the existing Japanese fortress room, navy physical playing mat, perspective, complete period card faces, brass and black lacquer interface, ivory Caudex body lettering and WeatheredQuill brush headings. Do not redesign as a website/dashboard. Use the right sidebar or an integrated low tray as specified, keep the visible battle and hand readable. Button outer corner cutouts reveal the background with no black corner artifacts. Text must be crisp, restrained and readable. No watermark. This is an illustrative design proposal, never evidence of implemented rules. Replace the right sidebar with PAY FOR THIS ACTION. Keep a compact full source-card preview at the top. Show 6 Gold required. Middle: source cards in an elegant compact vertical list; each retains a full miniature card face at left, and its available payment actions at right. One card named Seaside Bazaar has two independent selectable rows: Bow for Gold and Use Reaction — stays upright, to make it clear both can be available in the same payment. Use a subtle check and warm gold border on selected rows. Separate small caption Other ways to pay contains Destroy a Holding and Remove a card for a discount; these have a restrained rust-colored consequence line. At the bottom a stationary review receipt says 4 Gold + 2 discount / 6 cost, then Remove selected card from the game, then a Confirm payment button and a quieter Cancel action. Distinguish a discount from actual Gold. Avoid dense tiny grids, big new banners or excess explanation. Focus design on card-origin relationship and distinct actions. Produce a full wide game screenshot, not a multi-panel sheet.

concepts.title: B — Payment tray and receipt
concepts.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Edit the supplied native L5R Emperor game screenshot into a polished UI CONCEPT. Preserve the existing Japanese fortress room, navy physical playing mat, perspective, complete period card faces, brass and black lacquer interface, ivory Caudex body lettering and WeatheredQuill brush headings. Do not redesign as a website/dashboard. Use the right sidebar or an integrated low tray as specified, keep the visible battle and hand readable. Button outer corner cutouts reveal the background with no black corner artifacts. Text must be crisp, restrained and readable. No watermark. This is an illustrative design proposal, never evidence of implemented rules. Design an integrated PAYMENT tray along the bottom-right of the mat, above the hand, with a modest sidebar retaining the action source and cost. Wide tray offers four full card miniatures with legible footer ribbons Bow, Reaction, Destroy Holding, Remove for discount. Selecting an available mode glows the ribbon rather than obscuring artwork. A card that offers both Bow and Reaction has two distinct compact toggle ribbons. To the right of tray, narrow vertical receipt groups Gold contributed separately from Cost reduction: 4 Gold, 2 discount, 6 cost. Show exactly which selected Holding will be destroyed under Consequences and keep Confirm payment beside the receipt, Cancel secondary. Destructive/remove choices are clear muted red text without alarming modal styling. Preserve most of mat, avoid large central overlay or covering the hand. Labels Bow for Gold, Use Reaction, Destroy Holding, Remove for discount. All values illustrative. Create one full wide in-game screenshot.

concepts.title: C — Suggested payment, editable details

This is an illustrative design proposal, never evidence of implemented rules. Replace right sidebar with a calm compact payment inspector. Top source card and 6 Gold cost. Next an outlined brass selection titled Suggested payment with concise receipt 4 Gold + 2 discount. Under it selected source rows show full mini card scans, method and contribution. A link-like Change sources expands an accordion in the same sidebar showing other engine offered sources and their exact costs, including separate Bow and Reaction selections on one card. concepts.title: A — Source and consequence in sidebar
concepts.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Edit the supplied native L5R Emperor game screenshot into a polished UI CONCEPT. Preserve the existing Japanese fortress room, navy physical playing mat, perspective, complete period card faces, brass and black lacquer interface, ivory Caudex body lettering and WeatheredQuill brush headings. Do not redesign as a website/dashboard. Use the right sidebar or an integrated low tray as specified, keep the visible battle and hand readable. Button outer corner cutouts reveal the background with no black corner artifacts. Text must be crisp, restrained and readable. No watermark. This is an illustrative design proposal, never evidence of implemented rules. Replace HOW DO YOU PAY sidebar with ADDITIONAL ENTRY COST and source-card En'you at top; preserve the full scan styling but don't invent card text. State Your choice · Crane, then Remove a card from your hand, or destroy a Sake token. Two large option rows: Remove a hand card / Removed from the game, and Destroy a Sake token / Choose a token on your cards. Show first option selected with subtle outline. Under options show three full hand-card miniatures labelled Choose one card and highlight one in quiet teal/gold. Final review names Selected card → Removed from game in restrained rust. Confirm entry cost is fixed at bottom. Source preview explicitly separate from eligible choice cards, avoid using source card as candidate. Only current deciding seat sees candidates. Do not show cancel if cost is mandatory, don't include Back to target. Full wide game image.

Design ADDITIONAL ENTRY COST as a polished lacquer/brass tray integrated just above the hand along the bottom of the mat, no huge central modal. Sidebar is reduced to full source-card En'you preview and Your choice · Crane. Left end of tray identifies the source and prompt: Remove a hand card, or destroy a Sake token.
